Here is a clear breakdown for extensions that handle your content, writing, or browsing context. Extensions that process your content locally Grammar and writing: AI Writing Assistant for Firefox — Grammar checking and text rewriting runs in the browser using JavaScript. articles.title: I built a local-first bookmark manager that actually remembers what you saved
articles.excerpt: I saved links faster than I could find them again, so I built Linkit, a free desktop bookmark manager that fetches and summarizes every link as you save it. A browser bookmark stores a URL and nothing…
articles.body: I saved links faster than I could find them again, so I built Linkit, a free desktop bookmark manager that fetches and summarizes every link as you save it. A browser bookmark stores a URL and nothing else. That leaves three gaps: keyword search only matches exact titles, you have to open a link to know what it says, and the same article saved from three URLs looks like three entries. Linkit works on the saved content instead. What it does Summaries and key takeaways. Every saved link is fetched, summarized, and broken into a few takeaways. You scan the summary instead of opening twelve tabs. Point it at any OpenAI-compatible API, or run a local model through Ollama. Search that matches on meaning. Keyword search fails the moment you don't remember the wording.

articles.title: Background jobs that survive a closed tab need more than a queue
articles.excerpt: A browser can stop polling at any moment: its tab closes, the phone goes offline, or the user signs out. If the browser also owns the workflow, the work stops with it. A durable job changes that relat…
articles.body: A browser can stop polling at any moment: its tab closes, the phone goes offline, or the user signs out. If the browser also owns the workflow, the work stops with it. A durable job changes that relationship. The client asks the server to accept work, receives an identity, and later observes progress. Closing the screen stops observation, not the accepted job. The tricky failures occur between those steps: committing the job but failing to enqueue it, losing a worker halfway through a task, or letting an old worker write after a replacement has taken over. Commit admission before acknowledging it Create an owner-scoped job record and its initial tasks durably. Tie admission to an idempotency key so a lost acknowledgement can recover the same job.

articles.title: Converting Excel Workbooks to TIFF Images in Java: Use Cases, Mechanics, and Trade-offs
articles.excerpt: Excel workbooks are built for interactive use—formulas, multiple sheets, formatting, and embedded objects all live within a structured grid. TIFF, by contrast, is a flat, raster image format designed…
articles.body: Excel workbooks are built for interactive use—formulas, multiple sheets, formatting, and embedded objects all live within a structured grid. TIFF, by contrast, is a flat, raster image format designed for archival stability and consistent rendering across platforms. Converting between the two is less about convenience and more about solving specific problems: preserving the visual appearance of a spreadsheet for legal or regulatory archives, embedding tabular data into document management systems that only accept image formats, or generating fax-ready outputs from financial reports. This article examines the technical landscape of Excel-to-TIFF conversion in Java, using Spire.XLS for Java as a reference implementation.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
articles.body: On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes.

articles.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
articles.excerpt: New research suggests that Little Red Dots, which have puzzled astronomers since the JWST began discovering them, could host primordial black holes born during the Big Bang.
articles.body: Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium.

articles.title: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
articles.excerpt: "*sshole" poses a serious threat to Internet security.
articles.body: Hackers are actively exploiting a recently discovered critical vulnerability that allows them to log in to privileged accounts on many Linux systems, multiple researchers are reporting. The vulnerability, tracked under the name *sshole, arises from the interaction between OpenSSH and a code library known as musl. Linux systems that use both of these packages and meet certain other requirements can be hacked to give unauthenticated access to high-privilege accounts in a matter of seconds. *sshole became publicly known last Thursday and quickly stoked concerns it could lead to widespread compromise of Linux machines. Four days later, the prediction shows signs of becoming real.
